designDecisions.note: Locked with user 2026-10-18 — downstream agents (BA/TA/SA/QA) do NOT reopen these
designDecisions.D1: PREREQUISITE: refactor tabs -> per-tab sessions. Session-host registry key changes workspaceRoot -> workspaceRoot+tabId; per-tab token accounting + per-tab compaction (remove hardcoded tabId='default')
designDecisions.D2: Auto-run delivery model: inbound peer task AUTO-TRIGGERS receiving tab's agent turn (with mandatory anti-loop/rate guards, see AC3) — no human inbox approval
designDecisions.D3: In-memory PeerRegistry (tabId -> {agentName, role, capabilities, model, status}) + in-process PeerBus (EventEmitter-style): blocking request/response, async dispatch (fire + poll), per-pair conversation threads with bounded history
designDecisions.D4: New session tools (subject to FSD/TDD detail): peer_list(), peer_send(tabId, message, async?), peer_status(taskId) — shape-compatible with pi-a2a a2a_call(agent, message, async_dispatch?)/a2a_status so future cross-machine transport swap does not change the contract
designDecisions.D5: NON-GOALS: cross-machine/cross-window transport (pi-a2a's job), replacing pi-subagents or acp_delegate, mDNS/HTTP/gateway anything
designDecisions.D6: SEC-01 mitigation (Phase 3.7 conditions): Option A — full ToolApprovalGate fail-closed cho peer-triggered turns (TDD §7.6 recommendation; user deferred 'làm tiếp cho xong' → SM apply default 2026-10-20). Option B read-only loadout = future in-memory config; STC track B (TC-109) BLOCKED tại execution

suggestedAcceptanceCriteria: AC1: Two tabs in same window complete a blocking peer task exchange (A sends -> B auto-runs turn -> A receives reply) with zero configuration
AC2: Async dispatch returns task id; peer_status polls to terminal state
AC3: Anti-loop guard: per-pair turn cap (port pattern maxPingpongTurns=5 from pi-a2a) + per-tab rate limit; exceeded -> task fails with descriptive error, both tabs still functional
AC4: Peer-inbound activity visible in receiving tab UI (badge/indicator + transcript message prefixed like '[Peer inbound] from <tab>')
AC5: Peer messages pass through existing context governance (budget gate, auto-chunk, intra-turn guard) — no governance bypass
AC6: Per-tab sessions: each tab has isolated history + per-tab token accounting/compaction (no more hardcoded 'default')
AC7: Zero new config files/keys required for the local bus; no network sockets opened by the feature
AC8: Existing suites stay green (context-governance.*, auto-chunk, session routing tests)
